readout_other: BOLD fMRI of touch circuit (target and 5 off-target ROIs); MR-acoustic radiation force imaging (MR-ARFI) for FUS beam localisation
direction_notes: Concurrent med-FUS suppressed tactile-evoked BOLD activation at the target (area 3a/3b) and at all five off-target regions, while med-FUS alone (at rest, without tactile stimulation) directly excited neurons at the target and elicited BOLD activation in interconnected off-target regions; effects were state-dependent (active vs resting cortex).

timing.protocol_description: During fMRI acquisition, FUS pulses were delivered in a block design of seven 30 s FUS on/off cycles matched to the tactile stimulation blocks. During an 'on' block, a 300 ms pulse was emitted at 0.333 Hz (i.e. one 300 ms pulse every 3 s), giving 10 FUS bursts per on block. Each 300 ms pulse itself consisted of 63-cycle tone bursts repeated at 2 kHz (50% duty cycle). Tactile alone, tactile+med-FUS, and med-FUS alone conditions were interleaved within each fMRI run.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Two adult female macaque monkeys (M. fascicularis) were underwent six MRI experiments (three for each monkey).
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Two adult female macaque monkeys (M. fascicularis) were underwent six MRI experiments (three for each monkey).

flags.reason: Pulse duration (0.252 ms) computed from the stated 63-cycle burst at 250 kHz (cycles ÷ fundamental frequency), as explicitly permitted for this synonym of pulse duration.

The 0.333 Hz repetition rate of the 300 ms pulses within each 30 s on-block is a train-repetition interval, not the internal PRF field, and is described in protocol_description rather than the PRF field.
No sham or inactive-FUS control condition is described; comparisons are between tactile-alone, med-FUS-alone and tactile+med-FUS conditions.
